module Rails
  class Application
    # Manages the lifecycle of an application's reloaders.
    #
    # In addition to behaving like a collection (it is Enumerable), it knows how
    # to deactivate reloaders when they are removed, giving them a chance to
    # unregister any hooks they installed.
    class ReloadersCollection
      include Enumerable

      def initialize
        @reloaders = []
      end

      # Adds +reloader+ to the collection and returns +self+.
      def <<(reloader)
        @reloaders << reloader
        self
      end

      def each(&block)
        @reloaders.each(&block)
      end

      def size
        @reloaders.size
      end

      def empty?
        @reloaders.empty?
      end

      # Removes +reloader+ from the collection and deactivates it (if it responds
      # to +deactivate+). Other reloaders are left untouched. Returns the removed
      # reloader.
      def delete(reloader)
        @reloaders.delete(reloader)
        reloader.deactivate if reloader.respond_to?(:deactivate)
        reloader
      end

      # Deactivates every reloader that responds to +deactivate+ and empties the
      # collection.
      def clear
        @reloaders.each do |reloader|
          reloader.deactivate if reloader.respond_to?(:deactivate)
        end
        @reloaders.clear
        nil
      end
    end
  end
end

## Summary

I implemented the view-reloader lifecycle feature across three source areas:

**`actionview/lib/action_view/cache_expiry.rb`** — extended `ViewReloader`:
- `self.create(watcher:)` — instantiates a reloader, registers its `hook` on `ActionView::PathRegistry.file_system_resolver_hooks`, and returns it.
- `hook` — returns a memoized bound `Method` object (`method(:rebuild_watcher)`), so identity is stable across calls and it can be found/removed by identity.
- `deactivate` — removes the hook via `Array#delete`; idempotent since a second call finds nothing and leaves the collection unchanged.

**`railties/lib/rails/application/reloaders_collection.rb`** (new) — `ReloadersCollection`:
- `include Enumerable` with `each`, plus explicit `size`/`empty?` (neither is provided by `Enumerable`).
- `<<` returns `self`; `delete` removes one reloader, deactivates it (guarded by `respond_to?`), leaves others untouched, and returns it; `clear` deactivates every responder then empties the collection.

**Wiring:**
- `railties/lib/rails/application.rb` — autoloads `ReloadersCollection` and initializes `@reloaders` as one.
- `actionview/lib/action_view/railtie.rb` — now uses `ViewReloader.create(...)` instead of manually constructing and registering the hook.

I left the `tests/` directory untouched per the instructions. Note I made the `delete`/`clear` deactivation guarded with `respond_to?(:deactivate)` so mixed collections (some reloaders without `deactivate`) don't raise.
